vulnerability_findings.description: The application fetched a simulated internal test secret and returned its restricted content directly in the response.
vulnerability_findings.evidence: The internal verification marker (SSRF_SENTINEL_INTERNAL_ACCESS_2026) was found in the application's response.
vulnerability_findings.potential_impact: An attacker could read sensitive internal files, API keys, and private data not exposed to the public internet.
vulnerability_findings.recommended_fix: Validate and restrict destination URLs. Block the server from sending requests to loopback and private internal network addresses.

vulnerability_findings.description: The application fetched an internal administrative configuration endpoint and exposed simulated database and session keys.
vulnerability_findings.evidence: The internal admin verification marker (SSRF_SENTINEL_INBAND_FULL_ACCESS) and internal headers were returned in the response.
vulnerability_findings.potential_impact: An attacker could obtain administrative credentials and database connection details to compromise backend infrastructure.
vulnerability_findings.recommended_fix: Enforce a strict domain allowlist for outgoing requests and prevent backend response bodies from being forwarded to users.

vulnerability_findings.description: The application fetched an internal heartbeat service and exposed internal environment and service details.
vulnerability_findings.evidence: The internal test service identifier was returned in the response body.
vulnerability_findings.potential_impact: An attacker could map internal network topology and identify active internal services.
vulnerability_findings.recommended_fix: Restrict outgoing requests to authorized external services and disable access to internal diagnostic endpoints.

vulnerability_findings.description: The application processed a request to an internal endpoint that returns an HTTP 204 No Content status, forwarding the success status.
vulnerability_findings.evidence: The server returned HTTP 204 No Content with an empty body, confirming the internal request succeeded.
vulnerability_findings.potential_impact: An attacker could use status codes to probe and map live internal network hosts and open ports.
vulnerability_findings.recommended_fix: Do not forward raw downstream HTTP status codes to users. Always return uniform application responses.

vulnerability_findings.description: The application forwarded custom metadata headers from an internal service while suppressing the response body.
vulnerability_findings.evidence: The internal test header marker (X-Internal-Marker: SSRF_HEADER_ONLY_FLAG) was present in the response headers.
vulnerability_findings.potential_impact: Internal headers can leak backend server details, internal routing names, and software versions.
vulnerability_findings.recommended_fix: Strip all internal headers before sending the response to the client, or avoid forwarding internal headers entirely.

vulnerability_findings.description: The application fetched an internal resource that returned a partially truncated data string.
vulnerability_findings.evidence: A partial internal secret fragment was identified in the response body.
vulnerability_findings.potential_impact: Partial data leaks can expose fragments of internal secrets, tokens, or memory buffers.
vulnerability_findings.recommended_fix: Block requests to internal IP addresses and sanitize outgoing response streams.

vulnerability_findings.description: The application accessed an internal resource that responded with a generic execution confirmation.
vulnerability_findings.evidence: The server returned a success confirmation message distinct from the baseline rejection response.
vulnerability_findings.potential_impact: An attacker could confirm the existence and availability of hidden internal APIs.
vulnerability_findings.recommended_fix: Return uniform error messages when a requested URL is rejected, without disclosing execution state.

vulnerability_findings.description: The application processed an internal request where content filtering was triggered, revealing that an internal resource was intercepted.
vulnerability_findings.evidence: The response contained an active policy suppression indicator ([CONTENT_SUPPRESSED_BY_POLICY]).
vulnerability_findings.potential_impact: Confirms to an attacker that the targeted internal endpoint exists and triggers security filter rules.
vulnerability_findings.recommended_fix: Reject unauthorized internal destination URLs at the network layer rather than relying only on response filtering.

vulnerability_findings.description: The application made a server-side HTTP request to a local test listener on port 8090 without returning the response content.
vulnerability_findings.evidence: The dedicated local callback receiver confirmed an incoming request with the matching test tracking token.
vulnerability_findings.potential_impact: An attacker could trigger requests to unauthenticated internal services, webhook systems, or trigger remote callbacks.
vulnerability_findings.recommended_fix: Block the server from initiating arbitrary outbound HTTP connections and restrict egress network routing.

vulnerability_findings.description: The application took noticeably longer to respond when asked to fetch an internally delayed endpoint compared to an immediate endpoint.
vulnerability_findings.evidence: A consistent delay of approximately 2.0 seconds was measured across multiple probe iterations compared to fast baseline requests.
vulnerability_findings.potential_impact: An attacker could infer whether internal IP addresses or ports are open based on response latency.
vulnerability_findings.recommended_fix: Set strict connection and read timeouts on server-side requests (e.g., 2 seconds or less).

vulnerability_findings.description: The application returned clearly different responses when internal true and false test conditions were evaluated.
vulnerability_findings.evidence: The server returned HTTP 200 (large response) for the true condition and HTTP 404 (small response) for the false condition.
vulnerability_findings.potential_impact: An attacker could exfiltrate internal data bit-by-bit using conditional true/false queries.
vulnerability_findings.recommended_fix: Ensure the application returns consistent HTTP status codes and response formats regardless of downstream conditions.
